metadata.displayText:
Build a responsive, multilingual educational web application called VidyaGram, created by Team AROHA.

1. App vision
VidyaGram is an inclusive digital learning platform for government-school students and teachers, covering Classes 1–12. It should bring live classes, learning materials, virtual labs, AI assistance, attendance, assessments, and student progress into one easy-to-use platform.

The app must prioritize accessibility, simple navigation, low-data usage, and downloadable learning resources so students with limited internet connectivity can participate.

Create distinct experiences for students, teachers, parents or guardians, and school administrators. Each role should see only the information and tools relevant to them.

2. Login and onboarding
Provide role-based sign-up and login for students, teachers, parents or guardians, and administrators.

Allow students to join their class using a teacher-generated class code.

Treat the class code as a way to join a class, not as permission to view another student’s private information.

During onboarding, let users select their preferred language, school, class, and relevant subjects.

Let teachers create and manage classes, generate class codes, and manage enrolled students.

Allow parents or guardians to link to their child through a verified invitation or approval process.

3. Student dashboard and profile
Create a personalized student dashboard displaying:

Student name, school, class, and profile.

Upcoming live classes.

Attendance summary.

Marks, grades, and subject-wise progress.

Available learning materials and recent class recordings.

Pending quizzes and assessments.

Announcements and notifications.

Earned badges and class leaderboard position.

Provide a student profile page containing academic details, enrolled subjects, attendance history, assessment results, and achievements. Allow authorized users to update appropriate profile information.

4. Teacher dashboard
Create a teacher dashboard where teachers can:

Create and manage classes.

View enrolled students.

Schedule live classes.

Upload and organize educational resources.

Record and update attendance.

Create quizzes and publish assessments.

Enter or update marks and grades.

View student progress.

Respond to student doubts.

Send announcements and parent notifications.

Use an AI assistant for teaching-related tasks.

Updates made by teachers should appear in the relevant student dashboards.

5. Live classes and Zoom integration
Provide Zoom integration for scheduling and joining online classes.

Display each session’s subject, teacher, date, time, and joining link.

Allow teachers to attach supporting materials to a class.

Provide upcoming and completed class views.

Let teachers add recordings or recording links after a session.

Restrict class links and recordings to authorized users.

6. Recorded classes
Provide an organized library of recorded online classes.

Group recordings by class, subject, chapter or topic, teacher, and date.

Include search and filtering.

Allow students to replay lessons.

Support downloads where the teacher has enabled them.

Show recording availability clearly rather than displaying nonfunctional playback buttons.

7. Learning materials and assessments
Create a learning-resource section containing:

Notes.

Textbooks.

Model question papers.

MCQs.

Fill-in-the-blank questions.

Quizzes.

Revision materials.

Organize resources by class, subject, chapter or topic, language, and resource type.

Teachers should be able to upload, edit, organize, and publish resources. Students should be able to preview and download supported materials.

For quizzes:

Provide clear instructions and submission controls.

Automatically grade supported objective question types.

Show results, correct answers, and explanations when enabled by the teacher.

Save attempt history and update relevant progress information.

Allow teachers to control when results and answers become visible.

8. Virtual labs
Create a virtual-lab section for interactive, curriculum-related learning activities.

Organize activities by class and subject.

Include an objective, instructions, interactive activity, and a short understanding check.

Make controls easy to use on supported devices.

Provide lightweight alternatives where an activity requires substantial data or device resources.

Clearly distinguish working simulations from activities planned for a later release.

9. AI assistants for students and teachers
Provide separate AI-assistant experiences.

Student AI assistant:

Explain concepts in age-appropriate language.

Help students understand lessons and revision topics.

Guide students through problems step by step.

Help answer doubts about learning materials.

Support the student’s selected language where available.

Encourage understanding rather than only providing final answers.

Teacher AI assistant:

Help draft lesson plans.

Generate practice questions, MCQs, fill-in-the-blank exercises, and quizzes.

Draft summaries and revision notes.

Suggest simpler explanations for difficult concepts.

Help adapt teaching content for different classes and languages.

Label AI-generated content clearly. Allow teachers to review and edit generated material before publishing it. The assistant should acknowledge uncertainty rather than inventing information.

10. Attendance and parent notifications
Let teachers record and update attendance for each class.

Show students their own attendance history and percentage.

Let parents or guardians view attendance for their linked child.

Allow schools to configure a low-attendance threshold.

Notify linked parents or guardians when attendance falls below that threshold.

Record notification history and avoid sending repeated alerts unnecessarily.

Use in-app notifications, with optional email or SMS integrations if configured.

11. Marks, grades, and progress
Allow teachers to enter and update marks and grades by subject and assessment.

Display results on the student dashboard.

Show subject-wise progress using simple, understandable charts.

Let students and linked parents view relevant academic history.

Limit access to individual marks to the student, authorized teachers, linked parents, and administrators.

12. Digital library
Create a searchable digital library containing:

Storybooks.

Revision notes.

Supplementary educational reading.

Provide filters for class or age group, language, subject, and content type. Allow students to bookmark resources and download materials where permitted.

13. Doubt support
Provide a dedicated section where students can ask academic questions.

Allow students to add a subject, topic, question, and optional image attachment.

Let authorized teachers respond.

Offer AI assistance as a clearly labeled support option.

Let students track open and resolved doubts.

Notify students when a teacher replies.

Keep doubt discussions within the appropriate class or authorized audience.

14. Scholarship information
Create a scholarship-information section with:

Scholarship name and description.

Eligibility requirements.

Application deadline.

Required documents.

Official application link.

Last-verified or last-updated date.

Allow students to filter opportunities by relevant criteria, such as class and eligibility. Let administrators add and update listings, and clearly mark expired opportunities. Do not present sample scholarships as verified, real opportunities.

15. Multilingual experience
Include a visible language selector.

Design the interface to support English, Hindi, and additional regional languages.

Apply language preferences consistently across navigation, labels, and supported content.

Clearly indicate which languages are available for each learning resource.

Keep content readable and navigation consistent when users switch languages.

16. Offline access and low-data mode
Provide downloadable resources and a clearly labeled “Downloads” section.

Allow students to save supported notes, textbooks, revision materials, and permitted recordings for offline access.

Show which resources are available offline.

Let users remove downloaded resources.

Preserve supported offline activity and synchronize it when connectivity returns.

Explain which features require an internet connection.

Include a low-data mode that:

Disables video autoplay.

Prioritizes text and lightweight resources.

Uses compressed images where appropriate.

Offers lower-quality video or audio-only options when available.

Displays file sizes before downloads.

Do not imply that live classes, cloud AI, or every virtual lab will work offline.

17. Badges and leaderboard
Award badges for learning milestones, quiz participation, progress, and completed activities.

Provide a class-level leaderboard with clear scoring rules.

Encourage improvement and participation rather than displaying private academic records.

Let teachers enable or disable leaderboard participation.

Do not expose individual marks or sensitive student information publicly.

18. Feedback
Let students, teachers, and parents submit feedback.

Include categories such as learning content, technical issue, suggestion, and general feedback.

Provide an administrator view for reviewing and tracking submissions.

Show submission confirmation and, where applicable, resolution status.

19. Privacy, permissions, and administration
Make student privacy a core requirement.

Apply role-based permissions throughout the app.

Prevent students from accessing other students’ private records.

Restrict parent access to their linked child.

Protect personal information, attendance, grades, and private messages.

Provide secure authentication and appropriate account-management controls.

Avoid exposing student information through public profiles or leaderboards.

Include clear privacy information and suitable consent flows for student accounts.

Provide an administrator dashboard for managing schools, users, classes, resources, scholarship listings, feedback, and platform settings.

20. Design and navigation
Use a clean, welcoming, school-friendly visual design.

Make the app responsive for mobile phones, tablets, and desktops.

Use readable typography, good contrast, clearly labeled icons, and large touch targets.

Keep navigation simple for younger students and first-time users.

Include loading, empty, error, success, and offline states.

Avoid cluttered dashboards and unnecessary animation.

Suggested navigation:

Dashboard

My Classes

Live Classes

Recordings

Learning Materials

Quizzes

Virtual Labs

AI Assistant

Attendance

Marks and Progress

Digital Library

Doubt Support

Scholarships

Downloads

Notifications

Feedback

Profile and Settings

Adapt navigation to each user’s role rather than showing every feature to everyone.

21. Implementation expectations
Build a functional application, not just a landing page or static dashboard.

Use reusable components and a clear project structure.

Persist user records, class membership, resources, attendance, marks, quiz attempts, and feedback.

Connect related workflows: teacher updates should appear in the appropriate student and parent views.

Validate forms and handle errors clearly.

Use realistic, clearly labeled sample data for demonstrations.

Keep credentials and API keys out of frontend code.

Clearly identify integrations that require external configuration, including Zoom, AI services, and email or SMS.

Do not show fake success messages for actions that have not actually completed.

The final result should feel like one connected learning platform: students can join a class, access lessons, attend sessions, ask questions, complete quizzes, and track progress, while teachers can manage teaching and keep families informed.

content.text: No files found

Empty directory. Node 22 available. Let me plan the build.

I need to build a functional, responsive, multilingual educational web application. Given the scale, I should pick a pragmatic stack that runs offline without huge dependency installs. Options:

1. Next.js + React + Tailwind + Prisma/SQLite — heavy install, but powerful. Network availability unknown.
2. Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind + localStorage persistence — simpler, reliable, no backend needed. But requirement says "Keep credentials and API keys out of frontend code" and "clearly identify integrations requiring external configuration". A frontend-only demo with clearly labeled demo integrations is acceptable if we're transparent. But "Persist user records, class membership, resources, attendance, marks, quiz attempts, and feedback" — localStorage persistence works for a self-contained demo.
3. Full-stack with Express + SQLite (better-sqlite3 requires native build) — risky on Windows.

Let me check network availability for npm install first.

A great approach: Vite + React + TS + Tailwind, with a local API layer abstraction backed by localStorage (a "data store" simulating persistence). Include clearly labeled integration stubs for Zoom/AI/email/SMS. Add a small Express-free approach so it's a static app that can be deployed anywhere.

But heavy dependency install may fail. Let me test npm connectivity quickly.

Actually, I could build with React via Vite. Let me check network.

Let me think about quality bar and scope. This is a huge spec. I need to implement:

- Auth: role-based signup/login, class code join, parent link approval, teacher class management
- Student dashboard + profile
- Teacher dashboard: classes, students, schedule live classes, resources, attendance, quizzes, marks, progress, doubts, announcements, AI assistant
- Zoom integration (configurable, stub status)
- Recordings library with search/filters/download
- Learning materials & assessments
- Quizzes with auto-grading, attempt history, results visibility controls
- Virtual labs with real interactive simulations + marked planned ones
- AI assistants (student/teacher) — local rule-based fallback clearly labeled; configurable external provider status
- Attendance + parent notifications with threshold + dedupe + history
- Marks/grades/progress charts
- Digital library with bookmarks
- Doubt support
- Scholarships
- Multilingual (English, Hindi, + regional: Bengali/Tamil/Marathi/Telugu)
- Offline/low-data mode + Downloads
- Badges + leaderboard
- Feedback
- Privacy/RBAC/admin dashboard
- Design system, states, accessibility

That's a lot. I'll build carefully, with a well-structured multi-file React app.

Plan of architecture:

```
src/
  main.tsx
  App.tsx
  index.css
  lib/
    types.ts
    db.ts            // localStorage-backed store w/ seed data
    store.tsx        // React context, actions, selectors
    i18n.tsx         // translations + hook
    ai.ts            // local AI heuristics + provider status
    utils.ts
    seed.ts
  components/
    ui.tsx           // Button, Card, Badge, Input, Select, Modal, Tabs, EmptyState, Loading, ErrorState, ProgressBar, Chart...
    Layout.tsx       // sidebar, topbar, language selector, role nav
    ...
  pages/
    auth/Login...
    student/...
    teacher/...
    parent/...
    admin/...
```

Routing: use react-router-dom. It's small and reliable.

Persistence: localStorage with a seeded dataset, versioned. Include reset demo data.

Auth: password hashing via Web Crypto SHA-256 with salt (demo-level security, clearly noted). Session in localStorage.

Seed data: multiple teachers, students, classes, subjects, resources, quizzes, attendance, marks, doubts, scholarships (clearly labeled sample), recordings, labs, badges.

Charts: hand-rolled SVG to avoid dependency.

Let me now decide the language list: English, Hindi (हिन्दी), Marathi (मराठी), Bengali (বাংলা), Tamil (தமிழ்), Telugu (తెలుగు). Full UI translation for all 6 is a lot of strings. I'll do full English + Hindi, and for the others provide translation of core navigation/common labels with fallback to English for less-used strings, clearly indicated ("partial translations"). Actually the spec says "Design the interface to support English, Hindi, and additional regional languages" and "Clearly indicate which languages are available for each learning resource". So partial UI translation with a completion indicator is honest and reasonable. I'll do full English, full-ish Hindi, and substantial Marathi/Bengali/Tamil/Telugu for nav + common UI. Hmm, that's a huge amount of translation text written by me. I'll do nav + common actions in all; content-level for English/Hindi.

Let me be strategic: build a t() function with dictionary keyed by language; missing keys fall back to English. Provide ~200 keys for English, ~200 Hindi, and ~60-80 for each regional language covering nav + buttons + key headings. That's ~700 strings. Manageable if I'm efficient.

Actually to keep quality high and effort focused, maybe 5 languages: English, हिन्दी, मराठी, বাংলা, தமிழ். Add తెలుగు too — it's fine.

Let me first check npm install works.

Let me create the project with Vite manually (write package.json, then npm install).

Dependencies: react, react-dom, react-router-dom, vite, @vitejs/plugin-react, typescript, tailwindcss (v3 for stability with postcss/autoprefixer). Tailwind v4 changes config; I'll use v3.4.

Actually, do I need Tailwind? It speeds up styling a lot and is reliable. I'll use Tailwind v3 + a custom design token layer in CSS. Let's try install.

Let me run npm install in background maybe. First write package.json.

Let me carefully design data model:

```ts
type Role = 'student'|'teacher'|'parent'|'admin'

interface User {
  id: string
  role: Role
  name: string
  email: string
  phone?: string
  passwordHash: string
  salt: string
  language: Lang
  avatarColor: string
  schoolId: string
  createdAt: string
  // student
  classId?: string
  rollNo?: string
  guardianIds?: string[]
  // teacher
  subjectIds?: string[]
  // parent
  childIds?: string[]
  linkedStudentIds?: string[] // approved links
  lowDataMode?: boolean
  consentGiven?: boolean
  // admin
  isDemo?: boolean
}

interface School { id, name, code, district, state, lowAttendanceThreshold, settings { leaderboardDefault, contactEmail } }

interface ClassRoom { id, name, schoolId, teacherId, subjectIds, code, gradeLevel, section, createdAt, leaderboardEnabled }

interface Subject { id, name, nameKey?, color, classLevel? }  // maybe subject names per language
```

Subjects can be a fixed catalog with i18n keys: Mathematics, Science, English, Hindi, Social Science, Computer Science... Use subject ids: math, science, english, hindi, social, computer, evs.

Simplify: Subject catalog constants in lib/subjects.ts with translations by language via i18n keys `subject.math` etc.

```ts
interface Enrollment { id, classId, studentId, joinedAt, status }
interface Session { id, classId, subjectId, title, description, date (ISO), startTime, durationMin, teacherId, zoomLink?, zoomMeetingId?, status: 'scheduled'|'live'|'completed'|'cancelled', materials: resourceId[], recordingId? }
interface Recording { id, classId, subjectId, sessionId?, title, chapter, teacherId, date, durationMin, sizeMB, url?, downloadEnabled, quality: 'hd'|'sd'|'audio', provider: 'local'|'zoom', description }
interface Resource { id, title, type: 'note'|'textbook'|'question-paper'|'mcq-set'|'fill-blanks'|'quiz'|'revision'|'storybook'|'supplementary', classId, subjectId, chapter, topics[], language: Lang[], sizeKB, downloadable, published, uploadedBy, uploadedAt, content?, description, grades }
interface Quiz { id, classId, subjectId, title, instructions, published, dueAt, showResultsAt?, showAnswers: boolean, attemptsAllowed, timeLimitMin, questions: Question[], createdBy }
interface Question { id, type: 'mcq'|'fill', prompt, options?, answer, explanation, points }
interface Attempt { id, quizId, studentId, answers: Record<qid,string>, score, maxScore, submittedAt, graded: boolean }
interface AttendanceRecord { id, classId, date, subjectId?, period?, records: {studentId, status: 'present'|'absent'|'late'|'excused'}[], markedBy, updatedAt }
interface Assessment { id, classId, subjectId, title, type: 'unit-test'|'exam'|'assignment'|'project', date, maxMarks, published: boolean, createdBy }
interface Mark { id, assessmentId, studentId, marks, grade?, remarks?, updatedBy, updatedAt }
interface Doubt { id, studentId, classId, subjectId, topic, question, attachmentName?, status:'open'|'resolved', createdAt, replies: Reply[] }
interface Reply { id, authorId, authorRole, body, isAI, createdAt }
interface Announcement { id, classId?, schoolId, title, body, authorId, createdAt, audience: 'students'|'parents'|'all', pinned? }
interface Notification { id, userId, title, body, kind, createdAt, read, link? }
interface Scholarship { id, name, provider, description, eligibility, classes: number[], deadline, documents[], link, lastVerified, status: 'sample'|'verified', adminNotes }
interface Lab { id, title, subjectId, classLevels, objective, instructions, type: 'simulation'|'planned', simKind?: 'circuit'|'fraction'|'pendulum'|'ph-scale'|'solar'|'typing', dataMB, check: Question[], lowerDataAlternative }
interface Feedback { id, userId, role, category, subject, message, status: 'new'|'reviewing'|'resolved', createdAt, adminReply? }
interface DownloadItem { userId? in store per user: resourceId/recordingId, offlineAvailable, addedAt, sizeKB, kind }
interface ParentLink { id, parentId, studentId, status:'pending'|'approved'|'rejected', requestedAt, respondedAt, method:'invitation'|'code', studentConfirmedBy? }
interface Badge { id, key, nameKey, descKey, icon, criteria }
interface UserBadge { userId, badgeKey, awardedAt }
interface LeaderboardSettings per class + points from attempts/attendance/labs/downloads... compute score from activity.
```

Points: quiz score normalized, attendance present+2, lab completion +5, doubt resolved +3, badge +... Keep leaderboard based on XP not marks; show only first name + avatar + points. Teachers can disable per class. Students can opt out? "Let teachers enable or disable leaderboard participation." — class-level toggle in settings.

Zoom integration: `integrationConfig` in store with status from env: `zoomConfigured: false`, instructions. Since frontend-only, we cannot store secrets. const fractionsNote = `Fractions — comparing and ordering

A fraction shows a part of a whole. In 3/4, the denominator 4 tells us how many equal parts the whole is divided into, and the numerator 3 tells us how many parts we have.

1. Equivalent fractions
Multiply or divide both the numerator and the denominator by the same number.
3/4 = (3×2)/(4×2) = 6/8

2. Comparing fractions with the same denominator
The fraction with the larger numerator is greater: 5/8 > 3/8.

3. Comparing fractions with different denominators
Method A — common denominator: 2/3 and 3/5 become 10/15 and 9/15, so 2/3 > 3/5.
Method B — cross multiplication: 2×5 = 10 and 3×3 = 9. Since 10 > 9, 2/3 > 3/5.

4. Ordering on a number line
Convert each fraction to a decimal or a common denominator, then mark them from left to right. Smaller fractions sit closer to zero.

Practice
• Arrange 1/2, 2/5 and 3/10 from smallest to largest.
• Is 4/6 equal to 2/3? Explain using equivalent fractions.
• A roti is cut into 8 equal pieces. You eat 3. What fraction is left?

Remember: the denominator cannot be zero. A fraction greater than 1 can also be written as a mixed number: 7/4 = 1¾.`

const photoNote = `Photosynthesis — how plants make their own food

Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use sunlight, water and carbon dioxide to make glucose (food) and release oxygen.

Word equation
Carbon dioxide + Water --(sunlight, chlorophyll)--> Glucose + Oxygen

Balanced equation
6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂

Where it happens
Chloroplasts inside leaf cells. The green pigment chlorophyll absorbs light energy.

What is needed
1. Carbon dioxide — enters through tiny pores called stomata.
2. Water — absorbed by roots and carried up through the stem.
3. Sunlight — absorbed by chlorophyll.
4. Chlorophyll — the green pigment.

What is produced
Glucose is used for growth or stored as starch. Oxygen leaves through the stomata.

Why it matters
Photosynthesis produces the oxygen we breathe and is the starting point of almost every food chain. It also removes carbon dioxide from the air.

Think about it
• Why do leaves look green?
• What happens to photosynthesis at night?
• A plant kept in a dark cupboard for a week turns pale. Why?

Activity: place a leaf in sunlight for a day, then cover part of it with black paper for two days and test for starch with iodine (teacher supervision).`

const tensesNote = `Tenses made simple

Tense tells us when an action happens: past, present or future. Each has simple, continuous, perfect and perfect continuous forms.

Simple present — habits and facts
She walks to school every day. / They play cricket on Sundays.

Present continuous — happening now
She is reading a book. / They are waiting for the bus.

Simple past — finished actions
He visited his grandmother yesterday. / We finished the project last week.

Past continuous — an action in progress in the past
I was studying when the power went out.

Present perfect — past action with a present result
She has finished her homework. (So she is free now.)

Future — plans and predictions
We will visit the science fair tomorrow. / It is going to rain.

Common mistakes
✗ She go to school. → ✓ She goes to school.
✗ I am knowing the answer. → ✓ I know the answer.
✗ He did not went. → ✓ He did not go.

Practice
Underline the verb and name the tense:
1. The farmer is ploughing his field.
2. We have lived here for six years.
3. They will sing at the assembly.
4. I was writing a letter when you called.

Writing task: describe your morning routine in five sentences using the simple present. Then rewrite it in the simple past.`

const waterNote = `The water cycle

Water moves between the land, oceans and atmosphere in a continuous cycle.

Evaporation: heat from the sun turns surface water into water vapour.
Transpiration: plants release water vapour through their leaves.
Condensation: water vapour cools high in the atmosphere and forms tiny droplets, making clouds.
Precipitation: droplets join and fall as rain, snow or hail.
Collection: water gathers in rivers, lakes, ponds and underground.

Key terms
• Groundwater — water stored in spaces between soil and rock.
• Infiltration — movement of water down into the soil.
• Runoff — water that flows over the surface into streams.

Why it matters
The water cycle refills rivers and wells, moves heat around the planet and supplies fresh water for farming, drinking and industry.

In Sitapur: the monsoon rains fill ponds in July and August. When trees are cut down, less transpiration and more runoff can dry the soil faster.

Check yourself
1. What happens to water vapour when it cools?
2. Name two ways water returns to the atmosphere.
3. Why can a drought follow deforestation?`

const mapNote = `Reading maps and scales

A map is a drawing of a place seen from above, drawn to scale.

Essential parts
1. Title — what the map shows.
2. Scale — the relation between map distance and real distance. 1 cm = 5 km means 2 cm on the map is 10 km on the ground.
3. Direction — north is usually at the top. A compass rose shows N, E, S, W.
4. Key or legend — explains symbols and colours.
5. Grid — lines of latitude and longitude help locate places.

Types of maps
• Physical maps show mountains, rivers and plains.
• Political maps show states, districts and boundaries.
• Thematic maps show rainfall, crops, population or soil.

Measuring distance
If the scale is 1 cm = 25 km and two towns are 4 cm apart on the map, the real distance is 4 × 25 = 100 km.

Practice with the school map
1. Which direction is the playground from your classroom?
2. Measure the distance between Rampur and Bela in cm, then convert it using the map scale.
3. Find the symbol for a post office in the key.

Remember: a large-scale map shows a small area with more detail; a small-scale map shows a large area with less detail.`

const crowStory = `The Clever Crow / चतुर कौआ

One hot afternoon, a crow named Kalu was flying over a field in Rampur. He was very thirsty. His wings felt heavy and his throat was dry.

He looked everywhere. At last he saw a clay pot near a banyan tree. He flew down and looked inside. There was water at the bottom, but it was too low for his beak.

const mangoStory = `The Mango Tree Mystery

Every June, the giant mango tree behind the Bela school filled with fruit. Every June, the fruit disappeared before the children could count it.

const leavesStory = `Why leaves change colour

In summer, leaves look green because chlorophyll hides the other pigments. When autumn comes, shorter days and cooler nights break chlorophyll down. The yellow and orange pigments (carotenoids) that were there all along become visible. In some trees, red anthocyanins form from sugars trapped in the leaf.

This is why a single tree can show green, gold, orange and red in the same week. The tree is pulling useful nutrients back into its branches before the old leaves fall.

Try this: collect three leaves of different colours from the same tree. Compare their shapes and veins in your notebook.`

      marks: row.marks,
      grade: gradeFromPercent(pct),

/** Build leaderboard points from real activity in the seed. */
export const buildActivity = (): ActivityEvent[] => {
  const events: ActivityEvent[] = []
  let i = 0
  for (const day of ATTENDANCE.filter((d) => d.classId === 'cls_8a')) {
    for (const entry of day.entries) {
      if (entry.status === 'present' || entry.status === 'late') {
        events.push({
          id: `act_att_${i++}`,
          studentId: entry.studentId,
          classId: day.classId,
          points: entry.status === 'late' ? 3 : 5,
          reason: entry.status === 'late' ? 'attendance-late' : 'attendance-present',
          at: `${day.date}T15:30:00.000Z`,
        })
      }
    }
  }
  for (const attempt of ATTEMPTS) {
    const pct = attempt.maxScore ? attempt.score / attempt.maxScore : 0
    events.push({
      id: `act_quiz_${attempt.id}`,
      studentId: attempt.studentId,
      classId: 'cls_8a',
      points: 10 + Math.round(pct * 20),
      reason: 'quiz-attempt',
      at: attempt.submittedAt,
    })
  }
  for (const run of LAB_RUNS) {
    const cls = run.labId === 'lab_circuit' || run.labId === 'lab_ph' ? 'cls_8a' : 'cls_8a'
    events.push({
      id: `act_lab_${run.id}`,
      studentId: run.studentId,
      classId: cls,
      points: 8,
      reason: 'lab-check',
      at: run.completedAt,
    })
  }
  events.push({
    id: 'act_doubt_priya',
    studentId: 'usr_priya',
    classId: 'cls_8a',
    points: 4,
    reason: 'doubt-resolved',
    at: stamp(3, 10, 16),
  })
  return events
}

import type { DB } from '../types'
import { makeBase } from './base'
import { ATTEMPTS, QUIZZES, RECORDINGS, RESOURCES, SESSIONS } from './content'
import { ASSESSMENTS, ATTENDANCE, LAB_RUNS, MARKS } from './academic'
import {
  ANNOUNCEMENTS,
  AUDIT,
  BOOKMARKS,
  buildActivity,
  DOUBTS,
  DOWNLOADS,
  FEEDBACK,
  LABS,
  NOTIFICATIONS,
  PARENT_LINKS,
  SCHOLARSHIPS,
  USER_BADGES,
} from './community'

export const DB_VERSION = 4

export const SEED_STORAGE_KEY = 'vidyagram.db.v4'

/** Builds a fresh, internally consistent sample dataset relative to today. */
export async function buildSeed(): Promise<DB> {
  const base = await makeBase()
  return {
    version: DB_VERSION,
    seededAt: new Date().toISOString(),
    ...base,
    sessions: SESSIONS,
    recordings: RECORDINGS,
    resources: RESOURCES,
    quizzes: QUIZZES,
    attempts: ATTEMPTS,
    attendance: ATTENDANCE,
    assessments: ASSESSMENTS,
    marks: MARKS,
    doubts: DOUBTS,
    announcements: ANNOUNCEMENTS,
    notifications: NOTIFICATIONS,
    scholarships: SCHOLARSHIPS,
    labs: LABS,
    labRuns: LAB_RUNS,
    feedback: FEEDBACK,
    downloads: DOWNLOADS,
    parentLinks: PARENT_LINKS,
    userBadges: USER_BADGES,
    leaderboardOptOut: [],
    bookmarks: BOOKMARKS,
    outbox: [],
    activity: buildActivity(),
    audit: AUDIT,
  }
}

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build VidyaGram, a functional responsive multilingual educational web app for government-school students/teachers/parents/admins (Classes 1–12), credited to Team AROHA, with role-based dashboards, live classes, resources, quizzes, labs, AI assistants, attendance, marks, library, doubts, scholarships, offline mode, badges/leaderboard, feedback, and admin tools.

## Requirements
- Functional application, not a landing page; reusable components, clear structure.
- Persist users, class membership, resources, attendance, marks, attempts, feedback.
- Role-based permissions; students cannot see other students’ private records; parents only their approved-linked child; class codes join a class only.
- Multilingual UI (English, Hindi, + regional), visible language selector, honest language coverage per resource.
- Offline/low-data mode with downloads, sizes shown, sync on reconnect; never imply live classes/cloud AI/all labs work offline.
- Clearly label sample data and external-configuration needs (Zoom, AI, email/SMS); no secrets in frontend; no fake success messages.
- Teacher changes must appear in student/parent views; form validation and loading/empty/error/success/offline states.
- Responsive mobile/tablet/desktop; accessible typography, contrast, touch targets, labeled icons; navigation adapted per role.

## Decisions
- Stack: Vite + React 18 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS 3 + react-router-dom; localStorage persistence instead of a backend.
- Honest demo approach: integrations disabled in `public/config.js`, local rule-based AI labeled as demo, demo Zoom room opens an in-app labeled room, recordings without media show an unavailable state.
- Store exposes `mutate(fn)` over a cloned DB plus typed actions (login, signup, notify, awardPoints, awardBadge, queueOffline, syncOutbox, resetDemo, toast).
- Auth: salted SHA-256 via Web Crypto; demo password `demo1234`; sample accounts surfaced on login.
- Data model/seed built around Govt. Higher Secondary School, Rampur; Class 8-A (code `VIDYA-8A-2026`); student Aarav Sharma, teacher Meera Iyer, parent Sunita Sharma, admin Rakesh Verma; additional classes 7-B/6-A and parent Mahesh Patel linked to Nikhil.
- i18n split into `en.ts` (complete), `hi.ts` (complete), `regional.ts` (mr/bn/ta/te partial), with English fallback and published coverage percentages.
- Points/leaderboard based on activity only (attendance, quizzes, labs, resolved doubts), not marks; class-level leaderboard toggle.
- Quiz results visibility supports `immediately` / `after_due` / `manual` with `resultsReleased`.
- Seed dates generated relative to today; reset demo reseeds.

## Work State
### Completed
- Project scaffolding: `package.json`, Vite/TS/Tailwind/PostCSS configs; `npm install` succeeded (136 packages).
- `index.html`, `public/config.js`, `public/favicon.svg`, `public/manifest.webmanifest`.
- Domain model `src/lib/types.ts` (incl. AuditEntry, inviteCode, relationship, resultsReleased).
- i18n provider/dictionaries; subjects catalog; utils; access/privacy helpers; quiz grading; demo account helper.
- Seed data across `src/lib/seed/` (base, content, academic, community, index) with coherent relative dates, attendance, marks, quizzes/attempts, doubts, labs, scholarships, notifications, feedback, links, badges, activity, audit.
- Persistent store with auth, notifications, badges, offline outbox sync, toasts.
- Global CSS design tokens and icon set (`Icon.tsx`), reusable UI (`ui.tsx`), app shell/sidebar/topbar/language & profile menus (`Layout.tsx`), shared cards (`shared.tsx`).
- Login page and 3-step Signup/onboarding page.
- Student dashboard (`src/pages/dashboard/Student.tsx`).
- Announcement modal (`src/components/AnnouncementModal.tsx`).

### Active
- Building Teacher, Parent, and Admin dashboards next.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Create `src/pages/dashboard/Teacher.tsx`, `Parent.tsx`, `Admin.tsx`, and resolver `src/pages/dashboard/Dashboard.tsx`.
2. Create remaining feature pages: Classes, LiveClasses, Recordings, Materials, Quizzes + QuizRunner, Labs + LabDetail, AIAssistant, Attendance, Marks, Library, Doubts, Scholarships, Downloads, Notifications, Feedback, Profile, Privacy, Admin sections (schools/users/classes/content/approvals/scholarships/feedback/settings), ParentLink, Forbidden/NotFound.
3. Add `src/App.tsx` routes with auth/role guards and `src/main.tsx` (providers; optional service worker).

107: export const attendanceSummary = (db: DB, studentId: string, classId?: string): AttendanceSummary => {
108:   const relevant = db.attendance
109:     .filter((d) => !classId || d.classId === classId)
110:     .filter((d) => studentClassIds(db, studentId).includes(d.classId))
111:     .map((d) => ({ ...d, entries: d.entries.filter((e) => e.studentId === studentId) }))
112:     .filter((d) => d.entries.length > 0)
113:     .sort((a, b) => b.date.localeCompare(a.date))
114: 
115:   let present = 0
116:   let absent = 0
117:   let late = 0
118:   let excused = 0
119:   for (const day of relevant) {
120:     const status = day.entries[0].status
121:     if (status === 'present') present++
122:     else if (status === 'absent') absent++
123:     else if (status === 'late') late++
124:     else excused++
125:   }
126:   const total = relevant.length
127:   const attended = present + late
128:   return { present, absent, late, excused, total, pct: percent(attended, total), days: relevant }
129: }

285: const fractionsNote = `Fractions — comparing and ordering
286: 
287: A fraction shows a part of a whole. In 3/4, the denominator 4 tells us how many equal parts the whole is divided into, and the numerator 3 tells us how many parts we have.
288: 
289: 1. Equivalent fractions
290: Multiply or divide both the numerator and the denominator by the same number.
291: 3/4 = (3×2)/(4×2) = 6/8
292: 
293: 2. Comparing fractions with the same denominator
294: The fraction with the larger numerator is greater: 5/8 > 3/8.
295: 
296: 3. Comparing fractions with different denominators
297: Method A — common denominator: 2/3 and 3/5 become 10/15 and 9/15, so 2/3 > 3/5.
298: Method B — cross multiplication: 2×5 = 10 and 3×3 = 9. Since 10 > 9, 2/3 > 3/5.
299: 
300: 4. Ordering on a number line
301: Convert each fraction to a decimal or a common denominator, then mark them from left to right. Smaller fractions sit closer to zero.
302: 
303: Practice
304: • Arrange 1/2, 2/5 and 3/10 from smallest to largest.
305: • Is 4/6 equal to 2/3? Explain using equivalent fractions.
306: • A roti is cut into 8 equal pieces. You eat 3. What fraction is left?
307: 
308: Remember: the denominator cannot be zero. A fraction greater than 1 can also be written as a mixed number: 7/4 = 1¾.`

312: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use sunlight, water and carbon dioxide to make glucose (food) and release oxygen.

317: Balanced equation

378: const waterNote = `The water cycle
379: 
380: Water moves between the land, oceans and atmosphere in a continuous cycle.
381: 
382: Evaporation: heat from the sun turns surface water into water vapour.
383: Transpiration: plants release water vapour through their leaves.
384: Condensation: water vapour cools high in the atmosphere and forms tiny droplets, making clouds.
385: Precipitation: droplets join and fall as rain, snow or hail.
386: Collection: water gathers in rivers, lakes, ponds and underground.
387: 
388: Key terms
389: • Groundwater — water stored in spaces between soil and rock.
390: • Infiltration — movement of water down into the soil.
391: • Runoff — water that flows over the surface into streams.
392: 
393: Why it matters
394: The water cycle refills rivers and wells, moves heat around the planet and supplies fresh water for farming, drinking and industry.

396: In Sitapur: the monsoon rains fill ponds in July and August. When trees are cut down, less transpiration and more runoff can dry the soil faster.

403: const mapNote = `Reading maps and scales
404: 
405: A map is a drawing of a place seen from above, drawn to scale.
406: 
407: Essential parts
408: 1. Title — what the map shows.
409: 2. Scale — the relation between map distance and real distance. 1 cm = 5 km means 2 cm on the map is 10 km on the ground.
410: 3. Direction — north is usually at the top. A compass rose shows N, E, S, W.
411: 4. Key or legend — explains symbols and colours.
412: 5. Grid — lines of latitude and longitude help locate places.
413: 
414: Types of maps
415: • Physical maps show mountains, rivers and plains.
416: • Political maps show states, districts and boundaries.
417: • Thematic maps show rainfall, crops, population or soil.
418: 
419: Measuring distance
420: If the scale is 1 cm = 25 km and two towns are 4 cm apart on the map, the real distance is 4 × 25 = 100 km.
421: 
422: Practice with the school map
423: 1. Which direction is the playground from your classroom?
424: 2. Measure the distance between Rampur and Bela in cm, then convert it using the map scale.
425: 3. Find the symbol for a post office in the key.
426: 
427: Remember: a large-scale map shows a small area with more detail; a small-scale map shows a large area with less detail.`

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build VidyaGram, a functional responsive multilingual educational web app for government-school students/teachers/parents/admins (Classes 1–12), credited to Team AROHA, with role-based dashboards, live classes, resources, quizzes, labs, AI assistants, attendance, marks, library, doubts, scholarships, offline mode, badges/leaderboard, feedback, and admin tools.

## Requirements
- Functional application, not a landing page; reusable components, clear structure.
- Persist users, class membership, resources, attendance, marks, attempts, feedback.
- Role-based permissions; students cannot see other students’ private records; parents only their approved-linked child; class codes join a class only.
- Multilingual UI (English, Hindi, + regional), visible language selector, honest language coverage per resource.
- Offline/low-data mode with downloads, sizes shown, sync on reconnect; never imply live classes/cloud AI/all labs work offline.
- Clearly label sample data and external-configuration needs (Zoom, AI, email/SMS); no secrets in frontend; no fake success messages.
- Teacher changes must appear in student/parent views; form validation and loading/empty/error/success/offline states.
- Responsive mobile/tablet/desktop; accessible typography, contrast, touch targets, labeled icons; navigation adapted per role.

## Decisions
- Stack: Vite + React 18 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS 3 + react-router-dom; localStorage persistence instead of a backend.
- Honest demo approach: integrations disabled in `public/config.js`, local rule-based AI labeled as demo, demo Zoom room opens an in-app labeled room, recordings without media show an unavailable state.
- Store exposes `mutate(fn)` over a cloned DB plus typed actions (login, signup, notify, awardPoints, awardBadge, queueOffline, syncOutbox, resetDemo, toast).
- Auth: salted SHA-256 via Web Crypto; demo password `demo1234`; sample accounts surfaced on login.
- Data model/seed built around Govt. Higher Secondary School, Rampur; Class 8-A (code `VIDYA-8A-2026`); student Aarav Sharma, teacher Meera Iyer, parent Sunita Sharma, admin Rakesh Verma; additional classes 7-B/6-A and parent Mahesh Patel linked to Nikhil.
- i18n split into `en.ts` (complete), `hi.ts` (complete), `regional.ts` (mr/bn/ta/te partial), with English fallback and published coverage percentages.
- Points/leaderboard based on activity only (attendance, quizzes, labs, resolved doubts), not marks; class-level leaderboard toggle.
- Quiz results visibility supports `immediately` / `after_due` / `manual` with `resultsReleased`.
- Seed dates generated relative to today; reset demo reseeds.
- Download quota is demo-only 5 MB (`DEMO_STORAGE_LIMIT_KB`); resources are offline-readable only if they have `content`, recordings are metadata-only offline.

## Work State
### Completed
- Project scaffolding: `package.json`, Vite/TS/Tailwind/PostCSS configs; `npm install` succeeded (136 packages).
- `index.html`, `public/config.js`, `public/favicon.svg`, `public/manifest.webmanifest`.
- Domain model `src/lib/types.ts` (incl. AuditEntry, inviteCode, relationship, resultsReleased).
- i18n provider/dictionaries; subjects catalog; utils; access/privacy helpers; quiz grading; demo account helper.
- Seed data across `src/lib/seed/` (base, content, academic, community, index) with coherent relative dates, attendance, marks, quizzes/attempts, doubts, labs, scholarships, notifications, feedback, links, badges, activity, audit.
- Persistent store with auth, notifications, badges, offline outbox sync, toasts.
- Global CSS design tokens and icon set (`Icon.tsx`), reusable UI (`ui.tsx`), app shell/sidebar/topbar/language & profile menus (`Layout.tsx`), shared cards (`shared.tsx`).
- Login page and 3-step Signup/onboarding page.
- Student dashboard (`src/pages/dashboard/Student.tsx`).
- Announcement modal (`src/components/AnnouncementModal.tsx`).

107: export const attendanceSummary = (db: DB, studentId: string, classId?: string): AttendanceSummary => {
108:   const relevant = db.attendance
109:     .filter((d) => !classId || d.classId === classId)
110:     .filter((d) => studentClassIds(db, studentId).includes(d.classId))
111:     .map((d) => ({ ...d, entries: d.entries.filter((e) => e.studentId === studentId) }))
112:     .filter((d) => d.entries.length > 0)
113:     .sort((a, b) => b.date.localeCompare(a.date))
114: 
115:   let present = 0
116:   let absent = 0
117:   let late = 0
118:   let excused = 0
119:   for (const day of relevant) {
120:     const status = day.entries[0].status
121:     if (status === 'present') present++
122:     else if (status === 'absent') absent++
123:     else if (status === 'late') late++
124:     else excused++
125:   }
126:   const total = relevant.length
127:   const attended = present + late
128:   return { present, absent, late, excused, total, pct: percent(attended, total), days: relevant }
129: }

285: const fractionsNote = `Fractions — comparing and ordering
286: 
287: A fraction shows a part of a whole. In 3/4, the denominator 4 tells us how many equal parts the whole is divided into, and the numerator 3 tells us how many parts we have.
288: 
289: 1. Equivalent fractions
290: Multiply or divide both the numerator and the denominator by the same number.
291: 3/4 = (3×2)/(4×2) = 6/8
292: 
293: 2. Comparing fractions with the same denominator
294: The fraction with the larger numerator is greater: 5/8 > 3/8.
295: 
296: 3. Comparing fractions with different denominators
297: Method A — common denominator: 2/3 and 3/5 become 10/15 and 9/15, so 2/3 > 3/5.
298: Method B — cross multiplication: 2×5 = 10 and 3×3 = 9. Since 10 > 9, 2/3 > 3/5.

380: Water moves between the land, oceans and atmosphere in a continuous cycle.
381: 
382: Evaporation: heat from the sun turns surface water into water vapour.
383: Transpiration: plants release water vapour through their leaves.
384: Condensation: water vapour cools high in the atmosphere and forms tiny droplets, making clouds.

386: Collection: water gathers in rivers, lakes, ponds and underground.
387: 
388: Key terms
389: • Groundwater — water stored in spaces between soil and rock.

import type { Lang } from './types'

export interface StudyAnswer {
  title: string
  body: string
  steps: string[]
  followUp: string
  topic: string
}

const normalise = (value: string) => value.toLowerCase().replace(/[^\p{L}\p{N}\s/]/gu, ' ').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim()

const TOPICS: Array<{ keys: string[]; topic: string; build: () => StudyAnswer }> = [
  {
    keys: ['fraction', 'denominator', 'numerator', '2/3', '3/5', 'half', 'रोटी', 'भिन्न'],
    topic: 'Fractions',
    build: () => ({
      title: 'Comparing fractions',
      topic: 'Fractions',
      body:
        'A fraction shows part of a whole. The denominator (bottom number) tells how many equal parts the whole is cut into, and the numerator (top number) tells how many parts you have. A larger denominator means each piece is smaller, so 1/5 is smaller than 1/3.',
      steps: [
        'To compare 2/3 and 3/5, make the denominators the same. The lowest common denominator is 15.',
        '2/3 = (2×5)/(3×5) = 10/15. And 3/5 = (3×3)/(5×3) = 9/15.',
        'Because 10 > 9, we know 10/15 > 9/15. So 2/3 is greater than 3/5.',
        'You can also cross-multiply: 2×5 = 10 and 3×3 = 9. Since 10 > 9, 2/3 is larger.',
        'Try shading two rotis cut into thirds and fifths. Which shaded area is bigger?',
      ],
      followUp: 'Can you order 1/2, 2/5 and 3/10 from smallest to largest?',
    }),
  },
  {
    keys: ['photosynthesis', 'chlorophyll', 'stomata', 'plant food', 'प्रकाश संश्लेषण'],
    topic: 'Photosynthesis',
    build: () => ({
      title: 'How plants make food',
      topic: 'Photosynthesis',
      body:
        'Photosynthesis is how green plants use sunlight, water and carbon dioxide to make glucose (food) and release oxygen. It happens in the chloroplasts, which contain the green pigment chlorophyll.',
      steps: [
        'Carbon dioxide enters the leaf through tiny pores called stomata.',
        'Water is absorbed by the roots and carried up the stem.',
        'Chlorophyll captures light energy from the sun.',
        'The plant makes glucose and releases oxygen. Word equation: carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen (with sunlight and chlorophyll).',
        'At night, photosynthesis stops because there is no sunlight, but respiration continues.',
      ],
      followUp: 'Why do leaves look green? Think about which colour of light chlorophyll reflects.',
    }),
  },
  {
    keys: ['tense', 'past continuous', 'past perfect', 'was writing', 'had written', 'grammar', 'काल'],
    topic: 'Tenses',
    build: () => ({
      title: 'Past continuous and past perfect',
      topic: 'Tenses',
      body:
        'The past continuous describes an action that was in progress at a past moment. The past perfect describes an action that was completed before another past action. In “I was writing a letter when you called”, the writing was still happening when the call came, so “was writing” is correct.',
      steps: [
        'Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing. Example: She was reading when the power went out.',
        'Past perfect: had + past participle. Example: She had finished her homework before dinner.',
        'Ask: was the action still happening, or was it already complete? That decides the tense.',
        '“I had written a letter when you called” suggests the letter was already finished before the call. Different meaning.',
      ],
      followUp: 'Write one sentence about what you were doing when the school bell rang.',
    }),
  },
  {
    keys: ['water cycle', 'evaporation', 'condensation', 'rain', 'monsoon', 'जल चक्र'],
    topic: 'Water cycle',
    build: () => ({
      title: 'The water cycle',
      topic: 'Water cycle',
      body:
        'Water keeps moving between land, oceans and the air. The Sun heats surface water, plants release water vapour, the vapour cools into clouds, and the water returns as rain, snow or hail.',
      steps: [
        'Evaporation: heat turns surface water into water vapour.',
        'Transpiration: plants release water vapour through their leaves.',
        'Condensation: vapour cools high in the air and forms tiny droplets — clouds.',
        'Precipitation: droplets join and fall as rain, snow or hail.',
        'Collection: water gathers in rivers, ponds, lakes and underground.',
      ],
      followUp: 'Why can a drought follow deforestation? Think about transpiration and runoff.',
    }),
  },
  {
    keys: ['map', 'scale', 'direction', 'compass', 'नक्शा'],
    topic: 'Maps and scale',
    build: () => ({
      title: 'Reading a map scale',
      topic: 'Maps and scale',
      body:
        'A map is a drawing of a place seen from above, drawn to scale. The scale tells you how a distance on the map compares with the real distance on the ground.',
      steps: [
        'Find the scale, for example 1 cm = 25 km.',
        'Measure the distance between the two places on the map in centimetres.',
        'Multiply the map distance by the scale value: 4 cm × 25 km = 100 km.',
        'Check direction with the compass rose. North is usually at the top.',
        'Use the key or legend to understand symbols and colours.',
      ],
      followUp: 'If two towns are 3.5 cm apart on a map with scale 1 cm = 20 km, how far apart are they really?',
    }),
  },
  {
    keys: ['circuit', 'bulb', 'battery', 'current', 'conductor', 'विद्युत'],
    topic: 'Electric circuits',
    build: () => ({
      title: 'A simple circuit',
      topic: 'Electric circuits',
      body:
        'A bulb glows only when current can flow around a complete, unbroken path. The cell or battery provides the energy, wires carry the current, and the switch opens or closes the path.',
      steps: [
        'Connect the cell, switch, bulb and wires in one loop.',
        'Close the switch so the path is complete. Current flows and the bulb glows.',
        'Open the switch and the path breaks. Current stops and the bulb goes dark.',
        'Materials that let current pass are conductors (copper, iron). Rubber and plastic are insulators.',
        'Adding a second cell in the same direction increases the push, so the bulb usually glows brighter.',
      ],
      followUp: 'What would happen if you replaced the copper wire with a rubber band? Explain using the word insulator.',
    }),
  },
]

export function generateStudyAnswer(prompt: string): StudyAnswer {
  const text = normalise(prompt)
  for (const topic of TOPICS) {
    if (topic.keys.some((key) => text.includes(normalise(key)))) return topic.build()
  }
  return {
    title: 'Let us work through it',
    topic: prompt.trim().slice(0, 60) || 'Your question',
    body:
      'I could not find this exact topic in the class materials built into this demo, so I do not want to guess. Here is a reliable way to work it out, and your teacher can confirm the final answer.',
    steps: [
      'Write the question in your own words and underline the key word.',
      'Open the matching chapter in Learning Materials and look for that key word.',
      'Write what you already know, then what you are trying to find.',
      'Try one small example or diagram before solving the full question.',
      'If you are still stuck, send it to Doubt Support so your teacher can reply.',
    ],
    followUp: 'Which subject and chapter is this from? That will help me give a closer answer.',
  }
}

const cleanTopic = (topic: string) => topic.trim().replace(/\s+/g, ' ').slice(0, 90) || 'the topic'

export function generateTeacherDraft(kind: 'lesson' | 'questions' | 'revision' | 'simpler', topic: string, grade: number): string {
  const t = cleanTopic(topic)
  if (kind === 'lesson') {
    return `Lesson plan draft — ${t} (Class ${grade})
AI DRAFT · REVIEW BEFORE USE

Learning objective
By the end of the lesson, students can explain ${t} in their own words and apply it to one everyday example.

Prior knowledge (5 min)
Ask two quick questions about the previous chapter. Note students who need support.

Introduction (7 min)
Start with a local, concrete example connected to ${t}. Ask students to predict what will happen.

Guided practice (15 min)
1. Explain the key idea in three short steps.
2. Work one example together on the board.
3. Ask pairs to explain the idea to each other in their own language.

Independent practice (10 min)
Students solve two short tasks. Walk around and note common mistakes.

Check for understanding (5 min)
Exit ticket: one question on ${t}. Review answers before the next class.

Homework
One short practice task, plus reading the matching notes in Learning Materials.

Low-data alternative
Use the board and the printed note; no video needed.

Teacher notes
This draft is a starting point. Adapt the examples to your village and your students.`
  }
  if (kind === 'questions') {
    return `Practice questions draft — ${t} (Class ${grade})
AI DRAFT · REVIEW BEFORE USE

1. Define ${t} in one sentence.
2. Give one everyday example of ${t} and explain it.
3. True or false: ${t} works the same way in every situation. Justify your answer.
4. Apply: describe what would happen if one condition related to ${t} changed.
5. Draw and label a simple diagram showing ${t}.
6. Short answer: why does ${t} matter outside the classroom?

Answer guidance
Check definitions for the key terms, look for a correct example, and accept clear reasoning in the students' own words. Add marks for correct use of subject vocabulary.

Teacher notes
Edit the wording to match your textbook. Add a fill-in-the-blank version for students who need more support.`
  }
  if (kind === 'revision') {
    return `Revision notes draft — ${t} (Class ${grade})
AI DRAFT · REVIEW BEFORE USE

Key idea
${t} can be understood by breaking it into a cause, a process and a result.

Must-know terms
• Definition of ${t}
• Two examples
• One diagram or flow chart
• One common mistake to avoid

Quick recap
1. What is ${t}?
2. Why does it happen?
3. Where can you see it in daily life?
4. What is one exam-style question on it?

Memory aid
Turn the process into three short steps and practise saying them aloud.

Teacher notes
Check that the terms match the state textbook before sharing.`
  }
  return `Simpler explanation draft — ${t} (Class ${grade})
AI DRAFT · REVIEW BEFORE USE

Start with a familiar object or action.

Say it in three steps:
1. This is what ${t} means.
2. This is how it works.
3. This is why it matters.

Use one picture or one everyday example. Avoid new vocabulary until the idea is clear. Then ask the student to explain it back in their own language.

Teacher notes
Add the local-language version with a colleague before printing.`
}

/** The demo assistant never claims to be a live cloud model. */
export const demoAssistantNote = (lang: Lang): string =>
  lang === 'hi'
    ? 'यह डेमो सहायक इस डिवाइस पर एक छोटे नियम-आधारित मॉडल से चलता है। कोई बाहरी AI सेवा जुड़ी नहीं है।'
    : 'This demo assistant runs on-device with a small rule-based model. No external AI provider is connected.'

## Objective
- Build VidyaGram, a functional responsive multilingual educational web app for government-school students/teachers/parents/admins (Classes 1–12), credited to Team AROHA, with role-based dashboards, live classes, resources, quizzes, labs, AI assistants, attendance, marks, library, doubts, scholarships, offline mode, badges/leaderboard, feedback, and admin tools.

## Requirements
- Functional application, not a landing page; reusable components, clear structure.
- Persist users, class membership, resources, attendance, marks, attempts, feedback.
- Role-based permissions; students cannot see other students’ private records; parents only their approved-linked child; class codes join a class only.
- Multilingual UI (English, Hindi, + regional), visible language selector, honest language coverage per resource.
- Offline/low-data mode with downloads, sizes shown, sync on reconnect; never imply live classes/cloud AI/all labs work offline.
- Clearly label sample data and external-configuration needs (Zoom, AI, email/SMS); no secrets in frontend; no fake success messages.
- Teacher changes must appear in student/parent views; form validation and loading/empty/error/success/offline states.
- Responsive mobile/tablet/desktop; accessible typography, contrast, touch targets, labeled icons; navigation adapted per role.

## Decisions
- Stack: Vite + React 18 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS 3 + react-router-dom; localStorage persistence instead of a backend.
- Honest demo approach: integrations disabled in `public/config.js`, local rule-based AI labeled as demo, demo Zoom room opens an in-app labeled room, recordings without media show an unavailable state.
- Store exposes `mutate(fn)` over a cloned DB plus typed actions (login, signup, notify, awardPoints, awardBadge, queueOffline, syncOutbox, resetDemo, toast).
- Auth: salted SHA-256 via Web Crypto; demo password `demo1234`; sample accounts surfaced on login.
- Data model/seed built around Govt. Higher Secondary School, Rampur; Class 8-A (code `VIDYA-8A-2026`); student Aarav Sharma, teacher Meera Iyer, parent Sunita Sharma, admin Rakesh Verma; additional classes 7-B/6-A and parent Mahesh Patel linked to Nikhil.
- i18n split into `en.ts` (complete), `hi.ts` (complete), `regional.ts` (mr/bn/ta/te partial), with English fallback and published coverage percentages.
- Points/leaderboard based on activity only (attendance, quizzes, labs, resolved doubts), not marks; class-level leaderboard toggle.
- Quiz results visibility supports `immediately` / `after_due` / `manual` with `resultsReleased`.
- Seed dates generated relative to today; reset demo reseeds.
- Download quota is demo-only 5 MB (`DEMO_STORAGE_LIMIT_KB`); resources are offline-readable only if they have `content`, recordings are metadata-only offline.
- Local AI is rule-based in `src/lib/ai.ts` (`generateStudyAnswer`, `generateTeacherDraft`); demo assistant says no external AI provider is connected.

## Work State
### Completed
- Project scaffolding: `package.json`, Vite/TS/Tailwind/PostCSS configs; `npm install` succeeded.
- `index.html`, `public/config.js`, `public/favicon.svg`, `public/manifest.webmanifest`.
- Domain model `src/lib/types.ts`; i18n provider/dictionaries; subjects catalog; utils; access/privacy helpers; quiz grading; demo account helper.
- Seed data across `src/lib/seed/` (base, content, academic, community, index) with coherent relative dates, attendance, marks, quizzes/attempts, doubts, labs, scholarships, notifications, feedback, links, badges, activity, audit.
- Persistent store with auth, notifications, badges, offline outbox sync, toasts.
- Global CSS design tokens and icon set (`Icon.tsx`), reusable UI (`ui.tsx`), app shell/sidebar/topbar/language & profile menus (`Layout.tsx`), shared cards (`shared.tsx`).
- Login page and 3-step Signup/onboarding page.
- Student/Teacher/Parent/Admin dashboards and role resolver `Dashboard.tsx`.
- Announcement modal; offline helpers (`offline.ts`); Classes page; LiveClasses; Recordings; Materials; Quizzes list/builder.
- New `src/lib/ai.ts` rule-based study answers and teacher draft generator.
- New `src/pages/QuizRunner.tsx` (`/quizzes/:id`): teacher attempt review/release, student timed attempt, offline outbox queueing, result visibility.
- New `src/pages/Labs.tsx`: subject filters, working/planned labels, best-run badges.
- New `src/pages/LabDetail.tsx`: interactive fraction roti, circuit, pendulum, pH, place-value simulations, check questions, lab runs/points/badge.
- New `src/pages/AIAssistant.tsx`: on-device demo chat persisted per user, teacher draft tool, honest integration notices.
- New `src/pages/Attendance.tsx`: teacher marking/upsert, CSV export, low-attendance alert with 7-day guardian dedupe; student/parent summaries and history.
- New `src/pages/Marks.tsx`: teacher assessment creation/mark entry/publish with notifications; student/parent progress, grades, remarks, privacy notes.
- Fixed `RESOURCE_TYPES`/`RESOURCE_TYPE_LABEL` in `src/lib/subjects.ts` by removing invalid `'quiz'` entry.
- Added `@keyframes swing` to `src/index.css` for pendulum simulation.

### Active
- Building remaining feature pages: Library, Doubts, Scholarships, Downloads, Notifications, Feedback, Profile, Privacy, ParentLink, Forbidden/NotFound.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Create `src/pages/Library.tsx` with bookmarks, filters, reader, downloads.
2. Create `src/pages/Doubts.tsx` with student ask/offline queue, teacher reply/resolve, AI reply insertion.

683: /** Build leaderboard points from real activity in the seed. */
684: export const buildActivity = (): ActivityEvent[] => {
685:   const events: ActivityEvent[] = []
686:   let i = 0
687:   for (const day of ATTENDANCE.filter((d) => d.classId === 'cls_8a')) {
688:     for (const entry of day.entries) {
689:       if (entry.status === 'present' || entry.status === 'late') {
690:         events.push({
691:           id: `act_att_${i++}`,
692:           studentId: entry.studentId,
693:           classId: day.classId,
694:           points: entry.status === 'late' ? 3 : 5,
695:           reason: entry.status === 'late' ? 'attendance-late' : 'attendance-present',
696:           at: `${day.date}T15:30:00.000Z`,
697:         })
698:       }
699:     }
700:   }
701:   for (const attempt of ATTEMPTS) {
702:     const pct = attempt.maxScore ? attempt.score / attempt.maxScore : 0
703:     events.push({
704:       id: `act_quiz_${attempt.id}`,
705:       studentId: attempt.studentId,
706:       classId: 'cls_8a',
707:       points: 10 + Math.round(pct * 20),
708:       reason: 'quiz-attempt',
709:       at: attempt.submittedAt,
710:     })
711:   }
712:   for (const run of LAB_RUNS) {
713:     const cls = run.labId === 'lab_circuit' || run.labId === 'lab_ph' ? 'cls_8a' : 'cls_8a'
714:     events.push({
715:       id: `act_lab_${run.id}`,
716:       studentId: run.studentId,
717:       classId: cls,
718:       points: 8,
719:       reason: 'lab-check',
720:       at: run.completedAt,
721:     })
722:   }
723:   events.push({
724:     id: 'act_doubt_priya',
725:     studentId: 'usr_priya',
726:     classId: 'cls_8a',
727:     points: 4,
728:     reason: 'doubt-resolved',
729:     at: stamp(3, 10, 16),
730:   })
731:   return events
732: }

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build VidyaGram, a functional responsive multilingual educational web app for government-school students/teachers/parents/admins (Classes 1–12), credited to Team AROHA, with role-based dashboards, live classes, resources, quizzes, labs, AI assistants, attendance, marks, library, doubts, scholarships, offline mode, badges/leaderboard, feedback, and admin tools.

## Requirements
- Functional application, not a landing page; reusable components, clear structure.
- Persist users, class membership, resources, attendance, marks, attempts, feedback.
- Role-based permissions; students cannot see other students’ private records; parents only their approved-linked child; class codes join a class only.
- Multilingual UI (English, Hindi, + regional), visible language selector, honest language coverage per resource.
- Offline/low-data mode with downloads, sizes shown, sync on reconnect; never imply live classes/cloud AI/all labs work offline.
- Clearly label sample data and external-configuration needs (Zoom, AI, email/SMS); no secrets in frontend; no fake success messages.
- Teacher changes must appear in student/parent views; form validation and loading/empty/error/success/offline states.
- Responsive mobile/tablet/desktop; accessible typography, contrast, touch targets, labeled icons; navigation adapted per role.

## Decisions
- Stack: Vite + React 18 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS 3 + react-router-dom; localStorage persistence instead of a backend.
- Honest demo approach: integrations disabled in `public/config.js`, local rule-based AI labeled as demo, demo Zoom room opens an in-app labeled room, recordings without media show an unavailable state.
- Store exposes `mutate(fn)` over a cloned DB plus typed actions (login, signup, notify, awardPoints, awardBadge, queueOffline, syncOutbox, resetDemo, toast).
- Auth: salted SHA-256 via Web Crypto; demo password `demo1234`; sample accounts surfaced on login.
- Data model/seed built around Govt. Higher Secondary School, Rampur; Class 8-A (code `VIDYA-8A-2026`); student Aarav Sharma, teacher Meera Iyer, parent Sunita Sharma, admin Rakesh Verma; additional classes 7-B/6-A and parent Mahesh Patel linked to Nikhil.
- i18n split into `en.ts` (complete), `hi.ts` (complete), `regional.ts` (mr/bn/ta/te partial), with English fallback and published coverage percentages.
- Points/leaderboard based on activity only (attendance, quizzes, labs, resolved doubts), not marks; class-level leaderboard toggle.
- Quiz results visibility supports `immediately` / `after_due` / `manual` with `resultsReleased`.
- Seed dates generated relative to today; reset demo reseeds.
- Download quota is demo-only 5 MB (`DEMO_STORAGE_LIMIT_KB`); resources are offline-readable only if they have `content`, recordings are metadata-only offline.
- Local AI is rule-based in `src/lib/ai.ts` (`generateStudyAnswer`, `generateTeacherDraft`); demo assistant says no external AI provider is connected.
- Admin pages live in a single module `src/pages/admin/Admin.tsx`; `/admin/scholarships` reuses `ScholarshipsPage`, `/admin/feedback` reuses `AdminFeedbackPage`.
- Privacy page is accessible publicly via a gate that wraps it in `PublicShell` when signed out and `AppShell` when signed in; `AppShell` will need an optional `children` prop for this.

## Work State
### Completed
- Project scaffolding: `package.json`, Vite/TS/Tailwind/PostCSS configs; `npm install` succeeded.
- `index.html`, `public/config.js`, `public/favicon.svg`, `public/manifest.webmanifest`.
- Domain model `src/lib/types.ts`; i18n provider/dictionaries; subjects catalog; utils; access/privacy helpers; quiz grading; demo account helper.
- Seed data across `src/lib/seed/` (base, content, academic, community, index) with coherent relative dates, attendance, marks, quizzes/attempts, doubts, labs, scholarships, notifications, feedback, links, badges, activity, audit.
- Fixed missing `iso` import in `src/lib/seed/community.ts`.
- Persistent store with auth, notifications, badges, offline outbox sync, toasts.
- Global CSS design tokens and icon set (`Icon.tsx`), reusable UI (`ui.tsx`), app shell/sidebar/topbar/language & profile menus (`Layout.tsx`), shared cards (`shared.tsx`).
- Login page and 3-step Signup/onboarding page.
- Student/Teacher/Parent/Admin dashboards and role resolver `Dashboard.tsx`.
- Announcement modal; offline helpers (`offline.ts`); Classes page; LiveClasses; Recordings; Materials; Quizzes list/builder.
- New `src/lib/ai.ts` rule-based study answers and teacher draft generator.
- New `src/pages/QuizRunner.tsx` (`/quizzes/:id`): teacher attempt review/release, student timed attempt, offline outbox queueing, result visibility.
- New `src/pages/Labs.tsx`: subject filters, working/planned labels, best-run badges.
- New `src/pages/LabDetail.tsx`: interactive fraction roti, circuit, pendulum, pH, place-value simulations, check questions, lab runs/points/badge.
- New `src/pages/AIAssistant.tsx`: on-device demo chat persisted per user, teacher draft tool, honest integration notices.
- New `src/pages/Attendance.tsx`: teacher marking/upsert, CSV export, low-attendance alert with 7-day guardian dedupe; student/parent summaries and history.
- New `src/pages/Marks.tsx`: teacher assessment creation/mark entry/publish with notifications; student/parent progress, grades, remarks, privacy notes.
- Fixed `RESOURCE_TYPES`/`RESOURCE_TYPE_LABEL` in `src/lib/subjects.ts` by removing invalid `'quiz'` entry.
- Added `@keyframes swing` to `src/index.css` for pendulum simulation.
- Created `src/pages/Library.tsx`: search/filters, bookmarks tab, reader modal, download/bookmark actions with badge logic.
- Created `src/pages/Doubts.tsx`: student ask form with offline queueing, teacher/admin threads, replies, resolve/reopen, AI reply insertion, notifications and points.
- Created `src/pages/Scholarships.tsx`: sample/verification warnings, eligible-only filter, admin add/edit form with validation, audit logging.
- Created `src/pages/Downloads.tsx`: quota/storage display, resource reader, recording playback state, outbox sync/clear, CSV export.
- Created `src/pages/Notifications.tsx`: filters, mark read/all, preferences, honest email/SMS configuration states, quiet-hours toggle.
- Created `src/pages/Feedback.tsx`: form with offline queueing, own history with admin replies, plus exported `AdminFeedbackPage` inbox with status/reply management.
- Created `src/pages/Profile.tsx`: personal details validation, academic info, preferences/language/text size/low data/reduce motion, consent, guardian link approvals, badges, password change, data export, deletion request.
- Created `src/pages/ParentLink.tsx`: invitation-code linking, approval-request flow, linked children and link statuses.
- Created `src/pages/Privacy.tsx`: public-capable privacy notice, role permission table, consent/security/reporting sections.
- Created `src/pages/States.tsx`: `ForbiddenPage` and `NotFoundPage`.
- Created `src/pages/admin/Admin.tsx`: exports for schools, users, classes, content, approvals, settings, feedback, scholarships.
- Admin pages include school CRUD, user add/disable/export, class leaderboard toggles/codes, content publish/delete, guardian link approvals, platform settings/integration status/audit/reset.

### Active
- Creating `src/App.tsx` route tree and `src/main.tsx` providers.
- Need to modify `AppShell` in `Layout.tsx` to accept optional `children` so `/privacy` can render inside the authenticated shell.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Update `AppShell` to support optional `children` alongside `Outlet`.
2. Create `src/App.tsx` with public routes (`/login`, `/signup`, `/privacy` gate, fallback gates), authenticated `RequireAuth` layout, role guards, all feature routes, and admin routes.
3. Create `src/main.tsx` with `I18nProvider` outside `AppProvider`, then `BrowserRouter` and `App`; apply text-size/reduce-motion prefs and scroll restoration.
4. Add `docs/INTEGRATIONS.md` and `README.md` with demo accounts, setup, limitations, and integration contract.
5. Run `npm run build` / `npx tsc --noEmit`, fix TypeScript errors, then verify key role flows in browser.

## Relevant Files
- `src/lib/store.tsx`: app context/auth/persistence/offline sync; `useApp()` contract.
- `src/lib/types.ts`: canonical data model.
- `src/components/Layout.tsx`: `AppShell`/`PublicShell`/nav config; needs optional children prop.
- `src/lib/access.ts`: privacy gates, stats, leaderboard, quiz visibility.
- `src/lib/offline.ts`: download/quota/CSV helpers.
- `src/lib/ai.ts`: rule-based study/teacher draft generator.
- `src/lib/seed/index.ts` and `src/lib/seed/community.ts`: seeded DB; `iso` import fixed.
- `src/components/ui.tsx`: design-system components.
- `src/components/shared.tsx`: session/quiz/recording cards, leaderboard, badges.
- `src/pages/Profile.tsx`: preferences and consent patterns; password hashing/export helpers.
- `src/pages/Feedback.tsx`: exports `AdminFeedbackPage`, which `src/pages/admin/Admin.tsx` re-exports.
- `src/pages/Scholarships.tsx`: `ScholarshipsPage` reused by `/admin/scholarships`.

import { useEffect, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { Navigate, Route, Routes, useLocation } from 'react-router-dom'
import { useApp } from './lib/store'
import type { Role } from './lib/types'
import { AppShell, PublicShell } from './components/Layout'

import { LoginPage } from './pages/auth/Login'
import { SignupPage } from './pages/auth/Signup'
import { PrivacyPage } from './pages/Privacy'
import { Dashboard } from './pages/dashboard/Dashboard'
import { ClassesPage } from './pages/Classes'
import { LiveClassesPage } from './pages/LiveClasses'
import { RecordingsPage } from './pages/Recordings'
import { MaterialsPage } from './pages/Materials'
import { QuizzesPage } from './pages/Quizzes'
import { QuizRunnerPage } from './pages/QuizRunner'
import { LabsPage } from './pages/Labs'
import { LabDetailPage } from './pages/LabDetail'
import { AIAssistantPage } from './pages/AIAssistant'
import { LibraryPage } from './pages/Library'
import { AttendancePage } from './pages/Attendance'
import { MarksPage } from './pages/Marks'
import { DoubtsPage } from './pages/Doubts'
import { ScholarshipsPage } from './pages/Scholarships'
import { DownloadsPage } from './pages/Downloads'
import { NotificationsPage } from './pages/Notifications'
import { FeedbackPage } from './pages/Feedback'
import { ProfilePage } from './pages/Profile'
import { ParentLinkPage } from './pages/ParentLink'
import { ForbiddenPage, NotFoundPage } from './pages/States'
import {
  AdminApprovalsPage,
  AdminClassesPage,
  AdminContentPage,
  AdminSchoolsPage,
  AdminSettingsPage,
  AdminUsersPage,
} from './pages/admin/Admin'
import { AdminFeedbackPage } from './pages/Feedback'

const EVERYONE: Role[] = ['student', 'teacher', 'parent', 'admin']
const LEARNING: Role[] = ['student', 'teacher', 'admin']
const DOWNLOADS: Role[] = ['student', 'teacher']
const ADMINS: Role[] = ['admin']

function RequireAuth({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  const { currentUser } = useApp()
  const location = useLocation()
  if (!currentUser) {
    const from = `${location.pathname}${location.search}`
    return <Navigate to="/login" replace state={{ from: from === '/' ? '/dashboard' : from }} />
  }
  return <>{children}</>
}

function PublicOnly({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  const { currentUser } = useApp()
  if (currentUser) return <Navigate to="/dashboard" replace />
  return <>{children}</>
}

/** Route-level permission gate. Signed-in users without access see a clear explanation. */
function Allow({ roles, children }: { roles: Role[]; children: ReactNode }) {
  const { currentUser } = useApp()
  if (!currentUser) return <Navigate to="/login" replace />
  if (!roles.includes(currentUser.role)) return <Navigate to="/forbidden" replace />
  return <>{children}</>
}

/** The privacy notice can be read before signing in and stays inside the app afterwards. */
function PrivacyRoute() {
  const { currentUser } = useApp()
  if (currentUser) {
    return (
      <AppShell>
        <PrivacyPage />
      </AppShell>
    )
  }
  return (
    <PublicShell>
      <main className="mx-auto w-full max-w-wrap px-4 pb-10 sm:px-6">
        <PrivacyPage />
      </main>
    </PublicShell>
  )
}

function NotFoundRoute() {
  const { currentUser } = useApp()
  if (currentUser) {
    return (
      <AppShell>
        <NotFoundPage />
      </AppShell>
    )
  }
  return (
    <PublicShell>
      <main className="mx-auto w-full max-w-wrap px-4 pb-10 sm:px-6">
        <NotFoundPage />
      </main>
    </PublicShell>
  )
}

/** Applies per-account accessibility preferences to the whole document. */
function AppPreferences() {
  const { currentUser } = useApp()
  useEffect(() => {
